title: Two Crystal Springs golf leases and the rent the City collected

beats.text: A golf course on San Francisco water-system land received a rent credit it did not earn.

visual.sub: The public utility approved a mistaken base-rent credit

beats.text: Its accountant left the inflation adjustment out of the calculation.

visual.kicker: The public utility approved a mistaken base-rent credit

beats.text: The Controller confirmed the operator returned $23,683.

visual.label: The public utility approved a mistaken base-rent credit

beats.text: Ten late payments raised a different question.

visual.kicker: Ten late payments produced a separate dispute
Ten late payments produced a separate dispute

beats.text: It disputed the rest because the utility had usually enforced a later deadline.

visual.kicker: Ten late payments produced a separate dispute

beats.text: The City negotiated a new lease with the same operator, starting at $1 million a year.

visual.kicker: The next lease used different rent terms

beats.text: During the pandemic, the utility suspended payments while it negotiated possible relief.

visual.kicker: An informal rent suspension later left $981,640 to collect

beats.text: By the end of 2021, $981,640 had accumulated.

visual.label: An informal rent suspension later left $981,640 to collect

beats.text: The operator paid the entire later balance by February 2022.

visual.kicker: SFPUC collected the successor-lease balance in full
